prediction.mechanism_under_test: Whether the QUBO annealers' cost advantage over largest-remainder apportionment is partly an artefact of counting spin-wait in a thread-parallel solver.

expected.qubo_feasible_vs_balanced_quota: remains far above 100x. Point prediction: within +/- 25 % of the unpinned 288-290x, i.e. roughly 215-360x.
expected.qubo_tabu_vs_balanced_quota: qubo_tabu is wall-clock bounded, so its CPU-seconds should FALL by roughly the factor by which it was multi-threaded, if it was. This is the row most likely to move and the one to watch.
expected.exposure_parity_ties: balanced_quota still ties both annealers at 0.200 on all 900 paired user-records. Parity is an allocation property and must not move at all.
expected.intra_list_similarity: annealers still lower than balanced_quota's 0.3573, better on ~893 of 900 users. This is §10's surviving finding and pinning must not touch it.
expected.ndcg_identical: every accuracy figure bit-identical to rerankers_v2.

prediction.falsified_if: The qubo_feasible multiplier falls below 100x. That would mean a material part of §10's cost argument was spin-wait rather than work, and the section's central quantity would need restating. A fall in qubo_tabu alone is expected rather than falsifying, because its stopping rule is wall-clock: pinning changes how much CPU time one wall-clock second buys, which is a property of that solver and is already flagged in §10.
prediction.not_predicted: Absolute per-request costs. Whether qubo_tabu remains cheaper than qubo_feasible, since their relationship is set by a timeout rather than by work.
